info.name: VerseDB API Documentation
info.description: REST API for accessing comic book data, managing collections, and building integrations with VerseDB.

item.name: Discovery
item.description:
Dynamic content discovery endpoints for the home screen and new releases.

These endpoints provide curated and time-sensitive content like upcoming releases,
FOC (Final Order Cutoff) deadlines, and new first issues.

query.description: Results per page (1-50).
Page number; meta.last_page says where the list ends.
FOC window in days (1-30).
Start of FOC window (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.
Comma-separated publisher IDs; matches issues from any of them.
foc_date (default: FOC date, then publisher, then series name), publisher (publisher, then FOC date, then series name) or series (series name, then FOC date).
Keep only these languages in the `_i18n` maps (comma-separated BCP 47 tags). No other field changes.

request.description:
Returns issues with Final Order Cutoff (FOC) deadline within the next N days.
FOC is when retailers must place final orders with distributors (typically 2 weeks before release).

query.description: Lookback window in days (1-90).
Page number for pagination.
Items per page (1-50).
Keep only these languages in the `_i18n` maps (comma-separated BCP 47 tags). No other field changes.

request.description:
Returns recent releases from the titles, characters, creators, and teams the user
follows. A Series is not followable — it reaches this feed through its Title, and
every volume of that title counts.

`follow_contexts` and `follow_types` are top-level maps keyed by issue id: the
context explains why the issue is shown ("New in X-Men"), the type is one of
`title`, `character`, `creator`, `team`.

query.description: Results per page (1-50).
Page number; meta.last_page says where the list ends.
Lookahead window in days (1-90).
Keep only these languages in the `_i18n` maps (comma-separated BCP 47 tags). No other field changes.

request.description:
Returns upcoming first issues (#1) from new ongoing series within the next N days.
Useful for discovering new series launches.

item.name: Titles
item.description:
Endpoints for browsing comic book titles (franchises/properties).

A title represents a franchise (e.g., "Batman"), which may have multiple series under it.

query.description: Keep only these languages in the `_i18n` maps (comma-separated BCP 47 tags). No other field changes.

request.description:
Returns: id, name, slug, start_year, end_year, status, type,
image_url, content_rating_label, min_age, is_nsfw, imprint_id, series_count,
issues_count, average_rating, aliases

Use relationship endpoints for richer data:
- /titles/{id}/series - Get series in a title
- /titles/{id}/issues - Get issues across all series in a title
- /titles/{id}/creators - Get creators credited on the title
- /titles/{id}/characters - Get characters associated with the title
- /titles/{id}/teams - Get teams associated with the title

query.description: Search by title name.
Filter by publisher ID.

Comma-separated publisher IDs. Returns a title published by any one of them.
Return only titles whose start year has already arrived.

Comma-separated language codes. Returns titles with a series in any one of them.
Return only titles with an ongoing series. Combined with medium or languages, that same series has to match them.
Sort field. One of name, start_year, average_rating, cached_series_count, cached_issues_count; anything else falls back to name. Passing sort replaces the relevance ordering applied to q results.

Page number; meta.last_page says where the list ends.

request.description:
Returns full shop details including services offered.

`operating_hours` is keyed Monday-first by lowercase day name. Each value is
either `closed` or one or more 24-hour `HH:MM-HH:MM` ranges joined by commas
(a split shift reads `09:00-13:00,15:00-19:00`). A day missing from the map
has unknown hours — that is not the same as the shop being closed that day.

`special_hours` lists dated exceptions to the weekly hours, ordered by start
date: holiday closures, stocktake days, late openings for a release. Each entry
has `from` and `to` (inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD` dates, equal for a single day),
`hours` in the same grammar as `operating_hours`, and an optional `note`. On the
dates it covers, an entry replaces the weekly hours. Entries that have already
ended are left out, so an empty list means no exceptions are coming up.

item.name: Lists
item.description:
User-generated and curated lists of comic content.

Lists allow users to organize and share collections of issues, series, characters, creators, teams, or story arcs.
Users can save and like lists, and lists can be ranked or unranked.

**Entity Types:** issues, series, characters, creators, story_arcs, teams

**List Types:**
- `custom` - User-created lists
- `system` - Platform-curated lists (no owner)
- `wishlist` - User's default wishlist (cannot be deleted)

query.description: Search by list title or description, tolerating small typos in the title.
Filter by entity type (issues, series, characters, creators, story_arcs, teams). Matches lists declared as that type plus unrestricted lists holding at least one item of it.
Filter by who made it — `curated` for staff lists, `community` for everyone else. Omit for both.
Sort order (featured, newest, popular, most_saved). Default: featured.
Items per page (max 100).
Page number; meta.last_page says where the list ends.

request.description:
Returns paginated public lists with filtering and sorting options.
Only shows lists with at least one item.
Creates a new user list. A list filled by hand holds items of any type, so `entity_type` is ignored without a smart-list rule.

Sort order (newest, popular).

request.description:
Returns a user's public lists. Your own lists also include private and draft ones when the

query.description:
How to order the items. Omit for the list's own order — by
position when it is ranked, newest added first when it is not. `recent` and `oldest`
work on any list; the remaining values are the sortable fields for the list's entity
type (`name`, `release_date`, `start_year`, `issues_count`, `launch_date`, `arc_order`),
and are ignored on a mixed list, whose items span several tables.

request.description: Returns a single list with all its items. Private lists are only visible to owners.
Updates a list's metadata. Wishlists can only update privacy settings.
Permanently deletes a list and all its items. Wishlists cannot be deleted.
Saves a list to the user's saved lists for quick access. Cannot save your own lists.
Removes a list from the user's saved lists.

item.name: Like list, or react to it.

request.description: With no body this likes the list. Send `reaction` to leave that reaction instead, or to change the one already held; `DELETE` takes it back whichever it is. A member holds one reaction per list and every reaction counts toward `likes_count`. Cannot like your own lists.
Removes the user's like or reaction from a list.

item.name: Open a list to any type.

request.description: One-way: broadens a single-type list so it can hold items of any type. Existing items keep their own type. It cannot be narrowed back, and a wishlist already holds any type.

One-way: drops a smart list's rule and keeps every item the last refresh left, handing the contents back for editing by hand. A rule is only ever attached when a list is created, so it cannot be put back.

item.name: Merge a list into this one.

item.description:
Endpoints for looking up comics by barcode (UPC or ISBN) or by a distributor's
order code (Lunar or Universal). Used by the mobile app's barcode scanning feature
and exposed to User API tokens via the `lookup:barcode` ability.

On the Mobile API the GET lookups sit on the App Clip mode of the first-party
door: a signed-in session gets the full payload, and the App Clip, which has no
account, gets the preview payload with its attested clip token (#3044). On the
public User API they require the `lookup:barcode` token ability, and carry no
market quote.

item.name: Cover Lookup
item.description:
Identify a comic from a photo of its cover. The photo is matched by image against every cover
in the catalog (issues and variants), and the answer is catalog ids. No cover image is stored,
and none comes back beyond the cover URLs the issue resource already carries.

request.description:
Upload a photo of a comic cover (bare, bagged or slabbed) as `image`. `clear_match` true means
the image match is sure of the issue: `issue_id` is it, and `variant_id` is the cover when the
match also settled which of the issue's covers it is (null is the issue's own cover, or a cover
it could not tell apart from a same-art sibling such as a newsstand edition). `clear_match`
false means the image was not sure: `issue_id` is null and `candidates` lists up to five
issues it could be, best first, each at its best-scoring cover. Only the image is compared;
no text is read off the cover, so a slab label's grade is not returned. Requires the
`read:public` scope. Rate limited separately from catalog reads: 5/min and 100/day, or
15/min and 500/day on PRO.

item.name: Connect to VerseDB
item.description:
Lets a third-party site get a read-only token for a member's account without the member
copying one by hand. It is an OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with PKCE (S256).

1. Generate a random `code_verifier` (43-128 characters) and a `state`, and keep both on your
   server. The `code_challenge` is the base64url-encoded SHA-256 of the verifier, without padding.
2. Send the member to `https://versedb.com/connect` with `redirect_uri`, `state`,
   `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, and optionally `client_name` (your app, such as
   `WordPress`, 40 characters at most), `site_name` (100 at most) and `scope` (a space-separated
   subset of `read:public read:showcase`; both by default). `redirect_uri` must be HTTPS, or
   `http://localhost` while developing.
3. The member signs in if needed and approves or denies. VerseDB redirects to `redirect_uri` with
   `code` and `state`, or with `error=access_denied` and `state` when they deny. Check that
   `state` matches.
4. Within 5 minutes, exchange the code here from your server.

The token is named "{client_name}: {your host}", lasts 365 days, shows in the member's My Apps
page and counts toward their limit of 10 active tokens. Connecting the same site again replaces
its previous token. `read:showcase` reads the member's profile, collection, wishlist, pull list and
reading progress for display, without email, birth date, location, prices, notes, storage or loans.

item.name: Exchange a Connect code for a token

request.description:
Redeems the single-use code from the Connect redirect. A code works once: a second attempt,
a wrong `code_verifier` or a different `redirect_uri` fails and the code cannot be used again.
